finite_levels_provenance: The CMS convention level per point (lit-ew-blocks step 0): the largest relative finite deviation (d / max |Recola Laurent coefficient| of the row) of the neutral-only helicity rows (a right-handed u or d) of the electroweak-loop sectors QED^10 and QCD^4 QED^6 from Recola's polarised NLO (A/recola/polar_cms.f90), applied to every electroweak-loop sector; QCD^6 QED^4 its own neutral rows. The test compares each sector's full finite deviation relative to |finite| (the stricter reading) and at no less than the evaluation's default target accuracy stability.RESCUE_TARGET (the binary64 contract; Recola's own binary64 scatter is not bounded by pyAmpliCol's estimate), so QCD^6 QED^4 is checked at 1e-5. Deviation from the brief's (E0) per-sector definition, stated: by it QED^10 at point index 2 (4.92e-4) is 1 % above its own neutral-row level (4.87e-4), and QCD^2 QED^8 (<= 6.5e-4; its neutral rows hold no electroweak loop) is above the u u~ > d d~ control's CMS level (3.3e-4); both are shown convention-level by step 0's S2 demonstration (DECISIONS 2026-11-09 19:04): with every width scaled by lambda both fall as lambda^2 in both codes (4.92e-4 -> 4.97e-6 -> 4.98e-8; 6.52e-4 -> 7.28e-6 -> 7.38e-8 at lambda 1, 0.1, 0.01; u u~ > d d~: 1.5e-5 -> 1.5e-9), while the defect's residual (0.1 - 2.5) does not. The difference is the complex-mass prescription of the counterterms.
